## D. The signature on the deed

I believe Cesar's signature on the 29 September 2016 deed does not match his genuine signature [specimen I am comparing against: ____________]. I recognize that forgery is not pleaded, that my own affidavit (purposes (g)) says Cesar "execut[ed]" the deed, and that forgery must be proved by clear and convincing evidence. **I will not raise it on the stand.** If asked whether Cesar signed, I will say: "The deed presents itself as signed by Cesar as attorney-in-fact. I can't vouch for the signature. Even if it is his, he had no authority to sell to her."

What I ask is your assessment and, if you agree, this sequence: (1) a private questioned-documents examiner compares the deed (the original from Notary Donald E. Asis's records, Doc 304, Page 61, Book CXVI, s. 2016, or the Registry's registered copy) against genuine specimens of Cesar's signature from around 2016; (2) only if the examiner supports forgery, plead it in the alternative and ask for an NBI or PNP examination; (3) if not, we drop it quietly. Is there time before the defense presents in January?
